newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Swedish/Danish cigarette accord.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Swedish/Danish cigarette accord.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had approved a revised cooperation accord between Swedish Match Sverige and Danish company Skandinavisk Tobakskompagni concerning the Prince brand of cigarettes in Sweden.

"Following serious doubts expressed by the Commission as to the compatibility with the competition rules of their exclusive licensing arrangement, the two companies have come forward with a radical redefinition of their continued cooperation," the Commission said in a statement.
The Commission said those changes would lead to a structural overhaul of the Swedish cigarette market that would contribute to a "real and immediate increase in competition".
The parties said their cooperation would now take the form of two separate agreements for contract manufacture and physical distribution by Swedish Match until the end of 2001.

Swedish Match will manufacture Prince cigarettes sold by Skandinavisk Tobakskompagni on the Swedish market and handle the physical distribution of the cigarettes on a non-exclusive basis. Skandinavisk Tobakskompagni will have exclusive responsibility for sales, marketing and pricing of Prince in Sweden.
"These new arrangements should avoid any negative impact which might have resulted for either company from a more abrupt change," the Commission said.

The agreements will have the effect of placing essential control of Prince in the hands of the brand owner, Skandinavisk Tobakskompagni, while allowing it to continue benefiting from Swedish Match's manufacturing and distribution infrastructure, it said.
"This will effectively introduce a new competitor of considerable strength onto the Swedish cigarette market, thereby immediately increasing competition," it added. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
